beats.text: Japan never ran out of coins.
beats.note: Space Invaders was said to have drained the nation's 100-yen supply until the mint tripled production. The claim has been in print since 1980. Nobody checked it for thirty years.

beats.name: Tomohiro Nishikado
beats.role: He designed Space Invaders at Taito and engineered its hardware himself. The craze was real — the coin story grew on top of it, surfacing in foreign papers two years later.

beats.text: Production fell the year it launched.
beats.note: Japan struck 440 million 100-yen coins in 1977 and 292 million in 1978. The Bank of Japan, asked directly, could find no record of a shortage at all.
Fewer aliens meant the processor drew frames faster, so the survivors accelerated. Nishikado kept it — and the arcade difficulty curve was born as a hardware limit.

beats.text: Even Nishikado calls the coin story a rumour.
